Enlarge
ĕn-lärj´
v. (to make greater in size or room; to set at liberty; rendering Hebrew rachab, Greek platuno)
From en and large. The Hebrew behind it means to make broad, and Scripture uses it for a widened tent, a widened path under the feet, a widened heart, and a man given room when he was in distress.

Biblical Definition

To enlarge is to make room, and Scripture uses it for deliverance as often as for increase. Under pressure the Psalmist reports it as an act of God upon a confined man: “Thou hast enlarged my steps under me, that my feet did not slip” (Psalm 18:36). Broad footing rather than a narrow ledge is what keeps a man upright. Isaiah issues it as a command to a barren woman who is told to prepare for children she does not yet have: “Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes” (Isaiah 54:2). Faith enlarges before the increase arrives, and the command to strengthen the stakes belongs with it, since a wider tent needs deeper anchorage. Jabez prays for enlargement of territory and is granted it, though the prayer is bounded on either side by the presence of God's hand and preservation from evil: “Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil” (1 Chronicles 4:10). Paul uses the word for affection rather than acreage: “O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged” (2 Corinthians 6:11).

Webster 1828 Definition

To make greater in quantity, extent or room; to expand; to set at liberty. Scripture uses it of steps enlarged so the feet do not slip, of a tent widened in faith, of Jabez's coast, and of an apostle's heart enlarged toward a difficult church.

expand to see more

ENLARGE, v.t. [en and large.] To make greater in quantity or dimensions; to extend in limits, breadth or size; as, to enlarge a house or a field.

2. To expand; to dilate; to make more comprehensive; as, to enlarge the heart or the understanding.

3. To increase in appearance; to magnify to the eye.

4. To set free; to release from confinement or oppression; as, to enlarge a prisoner.

ENLARGE, v.i. To grow large or larger; to extend; to dilate; also, to expatiate; to speak or write at length upon a subject.

ENLARGEMENT, n. Increase of size or bulk; expansion; also, release from confinement or servitude.

Key Scripture

Psalm 18:36 — "Thou hast enlarged my steps under me, that my feet did not slip."

Isaiah 54:2 — "Enlarge the place of thy tent, and let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes;"

1 Chronicles 4:10 — "And Jabez called on the God of Israel, saying, Oh that thou wouldest bless me indeed, and enlarge my coast, and that thine hand might be with me, and that thou wouldest keep me from evil, that it may not grieve me! And God granted him that which he requested."

2 Corinthians 6:11 — "O ye Corinthians, our mouth is open unto you, our heart is enlarged."

Modern Corruption

The prayer of Jabez has been detached from its book and its terms and marketed as a technique for personal expansion, with the request for God's hand and for keeping from evil quietly dropped from the middle of it.

expand to see more

1 Chronicles 4:10 sits in the middle of nine chapters of genealogy, and the whole point of its placement is that God noticed one man in a list. The popular treatment reverses this, extracting the verse as a formula for enlargement and promising that repetition will produce increase. Two of the four petitions are usually neglected: that God's hand might be with him, and that he might be kept from evil so that it would not grieve him. A prayer for a wider coast without those two is a prayer for more territory than a man can hold without harm, and Scripture's own histories are full of kings whose borders grew and whose souls did not.

Isaiah 54:2 supplies the corrective picture. The command to enlarge the tent is given to the barren, before any children appear, and it comes paired with a second command — strengthen thy stakes. Enlargement without anchorage produces a structure that the first wind takes down, which is exactly what happens to ministries expanded faster than they are founded. Paul's use in 2 Corinthians 6:11 names the enlargement most worth seeking: a heart made wide toward a congregation that had wounded him. That kind of increase costs the man who receives it and injures nobody.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew rachab (to be or grow wide, to make room) supplies every Old Testament instance; Greek platuno (to make broad) renders the enlarged heart of 2 Corinthians 6:11.

expand to see more

Hebrew rachab (H7337) — to be wide, to enlarge, to make room; the verb of enlarged steps and an enlarged coast.

Hebrew merchab (H4800) — a broad place, room, liberty; the large place into which the LORD brings the delivered.

Hebrew gebuwl (H1366) — border, coast, territory; the thing Jabez asked to have enlarged.

Greek platuno (G4115) — to make broad, to enlarge; used of the enlarged heart and of broadened phylacteries.

Greek stenochoreo (G4729) — to be straitened, cramped; the opposite condition Paul names in the next verse.

Usage

"“Thou hast enlarged my steps under me” — room to stand is itself a deliverance."

"“Enlarge the place of thy tent… strengthen thy stakes” — widening and anchoring are commanded together."

"“Our heart is enlarged” — the enlargement most worth seeking is of the affections."
